newsitem.title: JAPAN: OLYMPICS-SUMO WRESTLERS TO FEATURE IN NAGANO OPENING CEREMONY.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-SUMO WRESTLERS TO FEATURE IN NAGANO OPENING CEREMONY.

text.p: Sumo wrestlers, naked from the waist up in sub-zero temperatures, and a globe-spanning chorus of "Ode to Joy" will feature in the opening ceremony for next year's Nagano Winter Olympics.
The proposed ceremony details were unveiled on the eve of the one-year countdown to the Games, to be staged about 200 kms west of Tokyo in the Japan Alps.
In a swipe at what the organisers called the "showy" and "senses-pounding extravaganzas" of previous games, Nagano said it planned a "simple, solemn and spiritual ceremony."
"It will be almost religious," one Nagano official said.
The announcement comes amid a flood of criticism of preparations for the last Olympic Games of the 20th century.

Skiing, the games highest-profile sport, wants a higher start for the men's downhill and floodlights for ski jumping. Ice hockey wants more seats. Figure skating wants better hotels. Alpine skiers want to lodge closer to their venues.

The Nagano Olympic Organising Committee (NAOC) is also under attack for failure to supply enough Western-style hotel rooms and for reneging on a promise to foot the entire bill of transport expenses for athletes.
But, for a while, criticism was far away in Thursday's multi-media presentation of what is planned for the two-hour opening ceremony.

Its main features are the giant sumo wrestlers, bare from the waist up in the sub-zero winter temperatures of February, and a chorus of "Ode to Joy" from the Fourth Movement of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony."
Choirs of 200 each in Beijing, New York, Sydney, Berlin, and Cape Town -- symbolising the world's five continents -- will join the main group of 2,000 in Nagano via a television satellite hookup.
The choir will be conducted by Japanese conductor Seiji Ozawa, for the past 13 years Music Director of the Boston Symphony Orchestra.
Giant trees also will be raised at the four points of the compass around the stadium in a traditional Japanese ceremony marking out its entrances.
Details of the lighting of the Olympic flame were not revealed.
"Games from the heart" will be the theme .... and it will feature events exemplifying a love of sports and love for humanity," a NAOC statement said.
The ceremony would "celebrate the magnificence of athletic achievement and not the wonders of special effects," it added.

The highlight of the wrestlers appearance will come when a top ranked "yokozuna", will stamp a traditional sumo ring where bouts are fought in a symbolic act to drive away evil spirits and purify the venue for the athletes.
